### 2. Conventions and notation

Let $(M,g)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension $n+1$ . Let $N\subset M$ be a compact domain with smooth boundary.

#### 2.1. Basic notations

We denote

- • $B_{r}(x)=\{y\in M\mid\mathrm{dist}_{g}(x,y)<r\}$ ,

- • $B_{r}^{N}(x)=B_{r}(x)\cap N$ ,

- • $A_{s,r}(x)=\{y\in M\mid s<\mathrm{dist}_{g}(x,y)<r\}$ ,

- • $A_{s,r}^{N}(x)=A_{s,r}(x)\cap N$ ,

- • $\mathcal{H}^{k}$ is the $k$ -dimensional Hausdorff measure on $(M,g)$ ,

- • $\mathrm{Int}(A)$ for $A\subset M$ is the union of all open sets $W$ in $M$ satisfying $W\subset A$ .

We say $U\subset N$ is relatively open if there is an open set $\tilde{U}\subset M$ with $\tilde{U}\cap N=U$ .

- • $\mathrm{int}_{\mathrm{rel}}(A)$ for $A\subset N$ is the union relatively open sets $U$ in $N$ satisfying $U\subset A$ .

#### 2.2. Varifolds

We denote

- • $\mathcal{V}_{k}(M)$ is the space of $k$ -varifolds in $M$ ,

- • $\mathcal{V}_{k}(N)$ is the space of $k$ -varifolds in $M$ with support in $N$ ,

- • $\mathbf{F}$ is the metric on $\mathcal{V}_{k}(M)$ given by

$$ \mathbf{F}(V_{1},V_{2})=\sup\{V_{1}(f)-V_{2}(f)\mid f\in C^{0,1}_{\text{cpt}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{k}(M)),\ |f|\leq 1,\ \mathrm{Lip}(f)\leq 1\}. $$

- • $\|V\|$ is the associated Radon measure on $M$ for $V\in\mathcal{V}_{k}(M)$ ,

- • $|\Sigma|$ is the integral $k$ -varifold associated to $\Sigma$ an immersed $k$ -dimensional submanifold,

- • $\|\Sigma\|$ is the associated Radon measure on $M$ for the $k$ -varifold $|\Sigma|$ , where $\Sigma$ is an immersed $k$ -dimensional submanifold,

- • $\delta V(X)$ is the first variation of the mass of $V\in\mathcal{V}_{k}(M)$ under the flow generated by the vector field $X$ ,

- • $\mathrm{VarTan}(V,x)$ is the set of varifold tangent cones at $x\in M$ for $V$ a $k$ -varifold with bounded first variation.

Let $\bar{\nu}$ denote the unit normal vector field along $\partial N$ pointing into $N$ . Let $U\subset N$ be relatively open. We denote

- • $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{cpt}}(U)$ is the space of smooth vector fields with compact support in $U$ ,

- • $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{cpt}}^{+}(U)=\{X\in\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{cpt}}(U)\mid\langle X,\bar{\nu}\rangle\geq 0\}$ .

Fix $c>0$ .

#### Definition 2.1 (Bounded constrained first variation).

$V\in\mathcal{V}_{k}(N)$ has $c$ -bounded constrained first variation in $U$ if

$$ \delta V(X)\geq-c\int_{U}|X|\ d\|V\| $$

for all $X\in\mathcal{X}_{\text{cpt}}^{+}(U)$ .

#### Definition 2.2 (Bounded first variation).

$V\in\mathcal{V}_{k}(N)$ has $c$ -bounded first variation in $U$ if there is an open set $\tilde{U}\subset M$ satisfying $\tilde{U}\cap N=U$ and

$$ |\delta V(X)|\leq c\|V\|(U)\|X\|_{C^{0}} $$

for all $X\in\mathcal{X}_{\text{cpt}}(\tilde{U})$ .

The following lemma is an adaptation of [Wan22, Lemma 2.6].

#### Lemma 2.3.

Let $V\in\mathcal{V}_{k}(N)$ have $c$ -bounded constrained first variation in $N$ . Then there is a constant $C=C(N,c)<\infty$ so that $V$ has $C$ -bounded first variation in $N$ .

#### Proof.

Let $r>0$ small enough so that the normal exponential map along $\partial N$ is a diffeomorphism. Extend $\bar{\nu}$ in $B_{r}(\partial N)$ by $\nabla_{\bar{\nu}}\bar{\nu}=0$ . Let $\eta\in C_{\text{cpt}}^{1}(B_{r}(\partial N),[0,1])$ so that $\eta\equiv 1$ in a neighborhood of $\partial N$ .

Let $X\in\mathcal{X}_{\text{cpt}}(M)$ satisfy $\|X\|_{C^{0}}=1$ (without loss of generality). Set $X_{0}=X-\eta\langle X,\bar{\nu}\rangle\bar{\nu}$ . By construction, $\pm X_{0}\mid_{N}\in\mathcal{X}_{\text{cpt}}^{+}(U)$ , $1\pm\langle X,\bar{\nu}\rangle\geq 0$ , and $|X_{0}|\leq|X|\leq 1$ . We compute

$$ \displaystyle\delta V(X) \displaystyle=\int(-\mathrm{div}_{S}(-X_{0})+\mathrm{div}_{S}(\eta\langle X,\bar{\nu}\rangle\bar{\nu}))\ dV(x,S) \displaystyle\leq c\|V\|(N)-\int(\mathrm{div}_{S}(\eta(1-\langle X,\bar{\nu}\rangle)\bar{\nu})+\mathrm{div}_{S}(\eta\bar{\nu}))\ dV(x,S) \displaystyle\leq c\|V\|(N)+c\|V\|(N)\|\eta(1-\langle X,\bar{\nu}\rangle)\|_{C^{0}}+\|\eta\bar{\nu}\|_{C^{1}}\|V\|(N) \displaystyle\leq(3c+\|\eta\bar{\nu}\|_{C^{1}})\|V\|(N), $$

and

$$ \displaystyle\delta V(X) \displaystyle=\int(\mathrm{div}_{S}X_{0}+\mathrm{div}_{S}(\eta\langle X,\bar{\nu}\rangle\bar{\nu}))\ dV(x,S) \displaystyle\geq-c\|V\|(N)+\int(\mathrm{div}_{S}(\eta(1+\langle X,\bar{\nu}\rangle)\bar{\nu})-\mathrm{div}_{S}(\eta\bar{\nu}))\ dV(x,S) \displaystyle\geq-c\|V\|(N)-c\|V\|(N)\|\eta(1+\langle X,\bar{\nu}\rangle)\|_{C^{0}}-\|\eta\bar{\nu}\|_{C^{1}}\|V\|(N) \displaystyle\geq-(3c+\|\eta\bar{\nu}\|_{C^{1}})\|V\|(N). $$

The conclusion follows by taking $C=3c+\|\eta\bar{\nu}\|_{C^{1}}$ . ∎

#### 2.3. Currents

We denote

- • $\mathbf{I}_{k}(M)$ is the space of $k$ -dimensional integral currents in $M$ ,

- • $\mathbf{I}_{k}(N)$ is the space of $k$ -dimensional integral currents in $M$ with support in $N$ ,

- • $[\Sigma]$ is the $k$ -dimensional integral current associated to an oriented immersed $k$ -dimensional submanifold of $M$ ,

- • $|T|$ is the associated integral $k$ -varifold for $T\in\mathbf{I}_{k}(M)$ ,

- • $\|T\|$ is the associated Radon measure on $M$ for $T\in\mathbf{I}_{k}(M)$ .

The space of integral currents has various norms and metrics:

- • $\mathbf{M}$ is the mass norm on $\mathbf{I}_{k}(M)$ ,

- • $\mathcal{F}$ is the flat norm on $\mathbf{I}_{k}(M)$ ,

- • $\mathbf{F}(T,S)$ for $T,S\in\mathbf{I}_{k}(M)$ is given by

$$ \mathbf{F}(T,S)=\mathcal{F}(T-S)+\mathbf{F}(|T|,|S|). $$

#### 2.4. Finite perimeter sets

We denote

- • $\mathcal{C}(M)$ is the collection of sets of finite perimeter in $M$ ,

- • $\partial^{*}\Omega$ is the reduced boundary for $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}(M)$ ,

- • $|\partial^{*}\Omega|$ is the integral $n$ -varifold associated to $\partial^{*}\Omega$ ,

- • $[\partial^{*}\Omega]$ is the $n$ -dimensional integral current associated to $\partial^{*}\Omega$ for $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}(M)$ .

$\mathcal{C}(M)$ naturally inherits 3 metrics from $\mathbf{I}_{n}(M)$ :

- • $\mathbf{M}([\partial^{*}\Omega])$ ,

- • $\mathcal{F}([\partial^{*}\Omega])$ ,

- • $\mathbf{F}([\partial^{*}\Omega_{1}],[\partial^{*}\Omega_{2}])$ .

By definition, we have

$$ \mathcal{F}([\partial^{*}\Omega])\leq\mathbf{F}([\partial^{*}\Omega],0)\ \ \text{and}\ \ \mathcal{F}([\partial^{*}\Omega])\leq\mathbf{M}([\partial^{*}\Omega]). $$

We recall the following fact when $M$ is closed, which can be found for instance in [IM18, Lemma 3.4].

#### Lemma 2.4.

There is a constant $\varepsilon_{0}>0$ (depending on $M$ closed) so that if $\mathcal{F}([\partial^{*}\Omega])\leq\varepsilon_{0}$ and $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega)\leq\frac{1}{2}\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(M)$ , then $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega)=\mathcal{F}([\partial^{*}\Omega])$ .

By (2.1) and Lemma 2.4, convergence in any of the above metrics implies $L^{1}$ convergence of the indicator functions of the finite perimeter sets.

#### 2.5. Hypersurfaces and mean curvature

Let $\phi:\Sigma\to(M,g)$ be a two-sided immersed hypersurface, and let $\nu$ be a continuous choice of unit normal vector field along $\Sigma$ . We let $H_{\Sigma,\nu}$ denote the mean curvature of $H$ with respect to $\nu$ . To specify our convention, for $\Sigma=\partial B_{1}^{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}}(0)$ and $\nu(x)=x$ (the outward pointing unit normal vector field for $B_{1}^{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}}(0)$ ), we have $H_{\Sigma,\nu}=n$ . In this convention, for a smooth vector field $X$ on $M$ , we have

$$ \delta|\Sigma|(X)=\int_{\Sigma}\langle X,H_{\Sigma,\nu}\nu\rangle d\|\Sigma\|. $$

If $\phi(\Sigma)=\partial\Omega$ , we write $H_{\Sigma,\Omega}$ to mean $H_{\Sigma,\nu}$ for $\nu$ the outward pointing unit normal vector field along $\Sigma$ .

#### Definition 2.5 (Almost embedding).

$\Sigma$ is almost embedded if for any $p\in\phi(\Sigma)$ where $\phi$ fails to be an embedding, there is a neighborhood $W$ of $p$ in $M$ so that $\Sigma\cap\phi^{-1}(W)=\sqcup_{i=1}^{N}\Sigma_{i}$ , $\phi\mid_{\Sigma_{i}}$ is an embedding for all $i$ , and for each $i\neq j$ , $\phi(\Sigma_{i})$ lies on one side of $\phi(\Sigma_{j})$ in $W$ .

#### Definition 2.6 (Prescribed/constant mean curvature).

For $h\in C^{\infty}_{\text{loc}}(M)$ , a two-sided immersion is an $h$ -PMC hypersurface if there is a choice of continuous unit normal vector field along $\Sigma$ satisfying $H_{\Sigma,\nu}=h\mid_{\Sigma}$ . If $h\equiv c$ constant, then $\Sigma$ is a $c$ -CMC hypersurface.

#### 2.6. Second variation and index

If $\Sigma=\partial\Omega$ is an $h$ -PMC hypersurface, then $\Sigma$ is a critical point44 4 Just like for the area functional, we can make sense of being a critical point over compactly supported variations even if the functional itself is undefined for $\Omega$ . for the functional

$$ \mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega^{\prime})=\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega^{\prime})-\int_{\Omega^{\prime}}h. $$

Let $\nu$ be the unit normal vector field along $\Sigma$ pointing out of $\Omega$ . The second variation of $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ for $\Sigma$ for any compactly supported normal variation $\varphi\nu$ is given by (see [Zho20, (1.3)])

$$ Q_{\Sigma}^{h}(\varphi,\varphi)=\int_{\Sigma}(|\nabla^{\Sigma}\varphi|^{2}-(\mathrm{Ric}_{M}(\nu,\nu)+|A_{\Sigma}|^{2}+\partial_{\nu}h)\varphi^{2}), $$

where $\mathrm{Ric}_{M}$ is the Ricci curvature of $(M,g)$ and $A_{\Sigma}$ is the second fundamental form of the immersion $\Sigma$ .

#### Definition 2.7 (Stability).

Let $U\subset M$ open. $\Sigma$ is $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -stable in $U$ if $Q_{\Sigma}^{h}$ is positive semi-definite on $C^{\infty}_{\text{cpt}}(U)$ (otherwise $\Sigma$ is $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -unstable). $\Sigma$ is strictly $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -stable in $U$ if $Q_{\Sigma}^{h}$ is positive definite on $C^{\infty}_{\text{cpt}}(U)$ .

#### Definition 2.8 (Index).

Let $U\subset M$ open. We define

$$ \mathrm{index}_{\mathcal{A}^{h},U}(\Sigma)=\sup\{\mathrm{dim}(L)\mid L\text{\ is a subspace of\ }C^{\infty}_{\text{cpt}}(U),\ Q_{\Sigma}^{h}\mid_{L}\text{is negative definite}\}. $$

If $U=M$ , we omit $U$ from the subscript.

#### Definition 2.9 (Nondegenerate).

Suppose $\Sigma$ is closed. $\Sigma$ is $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -nondegenerate if the operator

$$ \mathcal{L}_{\Sigma}^{h}=-\Delta_{\Sigma}-(\mathrm{Ric}_{M}(\nu,\nu)+|A_{\Sigma}|^{2}+\partial_{\nu}h) $$

has trivial kernel55 5 If $\Sigma$ is nondegenerate and stable, then $\Sigma$ is strictly stable..

## Part I Compact Manifolds with Barrier

In this part of the paper, we develop the tools for a localized min-max theorem in compact manifolds whose boundary provides a good barrier.

### 3. Setup

Let $(N,\partial N,g)$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary. We always assume that the dimension of $N$ is $3\leq n+1\leq 7$ .

Let $(\tilde{N},\tilde{g})$ be a smooth closed Riemannian manifold of dimesion $n+1$ which contains $(N,\partial N,g)$ isometrically.

#### 3.1. Space of subsets

We fix a disjoint decomposition by connected components $\tilde{N}\setminus N=E_{+}\sqcup E_{-}$ and let $P_{\pm}=\partial E_{\pm}$ .

We let $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ denote the set of all $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}(\tilde{N})$ satisfying

$$ E_{+}\subset\Omega\ \ \text{and}\ \ E_{-}\cap\Omega=\varnothing. $$

Note that $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ naturally inherits any metric or topology on $\mathcal{C}(\tilde{N})$ .

#### 3.2. Functional

Fix $h\in C^{\infty}(N)$ . In an abuse of notation, we also let $h$ denote a fixed smooth extension of $h$ to $\tilde{N}$ . We let $c:=\sup_{\tilde{N}}|h|$ . For $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ , we define

$$ \mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)=\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)-\int_{\Omega}h. $$

#### 3.3. Barrier

We define what it means for $\partial N$ to be a good barrier for min-max constructions for $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ over $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ .

#### Definition 3.1.

$\partial N$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+},P_{-})$ if

$$ H_{P_{+},E_{+}}<h\mid_{P_{+}}\ \ \text{and}\ \ H_{P_{-},E_{-}}<-h\mid_{P_{-}}. $$

#### 3.4. Min-max setup

Let $X^{k}$ be a connected cubical complex of dimension $k$ in some $I^{m}=[0,1]^{m}$ . Let $Z\subset X$ be a nonempty cubical subcomplex.

Let $\Phi_{0}:X\to\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ be a continuous map in the $\mathbf{F}$ -topology66 6 We can assume, without loss of generality by [Mag12, Remarks 15.2 and 15.3], that $\partial\Phi_{0}(x)=\overline{\partial^{*}\Phi_{0}(x)}$ for all $x\in X$ ..

#### Definition 3.2 (Homotopy class).

Let $\Pi$ be the set of all sequences of $\mathbf{F}$ -continuous maps $\{\Phi_{i}:X\to\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)\}_{i}$ so that there are $\mathcal{F}$ -continuous homotopies $\{\Psi_{i}:[0,1]\times X\to\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)\}_{i}$ satisfying $\Psi_{i}(0,\cdot)=\Phi_{i}$ , $\Psi_{i}(1,\cdot)=\Phi_{0}$ , and

$$ \limsup_{i\to\infty}\sup\{\mathbf{F}(\Psi_{i}(t,z),\Phi_{0}(z))\mid t\in[0,1],\ z\in Z\}=0. $$

Such a sequence $\{\Phi_{i}\}$ is called an $(X,Z)$ -homotopy sequence of mappings to $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ , and $\Pi$ is called the $(X,Z)$ -homotopy class of $\Phi_{0}$ .

#### Definition 3.3 (Width).

The $h$ -width of $\Pi$ is

$$ \mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)=\inf_{\{\Phi_{i}\}\in\Pi}\limsup_{i\to\infty}\sup_{x\in X}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{i}(x)). $$

#### Definition 3.4 (Minimizing sequence).

We say $\{\Phi_{i}\}_{i}\in\Pi$ is a minimizing sequence if

$$ \limsup_{i\to\infty}\sup_{x\in X}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{i}(x))=\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi). $$

#### Definition 3.5 (Critical set).

The critical set of a minimizing sequence $\{\Phi_{i}\}_{i}\in\Pi$ is

$$ \mathbf{C}(\{\Phi_{i}\})=\left\{V\in\mathcal{V}_{n}(N)\mid V=\lim_{j\to\infty}|\partial^{*}\Phi_{i_{j}}(x_{j})|,\ \lim_{j\to\infty}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{i_{j}}(x_{j}))=\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Phi)\right\}. $$

### 4. Preliminary tools

Here we collect the standard facts required for the min-max construction.

#### 4.1. Local regularity for obstacle problem

We recall that the dimension of $N$ is assumed to be $3\leq n+1\leq 7$ .

#### Theorem 4.1.

Let $U\subset N$ be relatively open. Suppose $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ minimizes $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ in $\{\Omega^{\prime}\in\mathcal{C}(\tilde{N})\mid\Omega\triangle\Omega^{\prime}\subset\subset U\}\subset\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ . Then $\partial^{*}\Omega\cap U=\partial\Omega\cap U$ is a $C^{1,\alpha}$ embedded hypersurface in $U$ .

#### Proof.

Let $\Omega^{\prime}\subset\mathcal{C}(\tilde{N})$ satisfy $\Omega\triangle\Omega^{\prime}\subset B_{r}(x)\cap N\subset U$ . Then

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)-\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega^{\prime}) \displaystyle=\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)-\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega^{\prime})+\int_{\Omega}h-\int_{\Omega^{\prime}}h \displaystyle\leq\int_{\Omega\setminus\Omega^{\prime}}h-\int_{\Omega^{\prime}\setminus\Omega}h \displaystyle\leq c\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(B_{r}(x)) \displaystyle\leq c\omega r^{n+1}, $$

where $\omega$ is a constant depending on $(N,g)$ and $r_{0}$ for all $r<r_{0}$ . In other words, $\Omega$ is almost minimizing with respect to the obstacle $\partial N$ . Hence, the arguments of [Tam82, §3] apply to give the desired regularity (working only in the assumed dimensions). ∎

When $\partial N$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+},P_{-})$ , we use the maximum principle and the above $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity to show that local $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -minimizers lie in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ .

#### Corollary 4.2.

Let $U\subset N$ be relatively open. Suppose $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ minimizes $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ in $\{\Omega^{\prime}\in\mathcal{C}(\tilde{N})\mid\Omega\triangle\Omega^{\prime}\subset\subset U\}\subset\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ . Further suppose that $\partial N$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+},P_{-})$ . Then $\partial^{*}\Omega\cap U=\partial\Omega\cap U$ is a smooth embedded $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -stable hypersurface in $U\cap\mathrm{Int}(N)$ with $H_{\partial\Omega,\Omega}=h\mid_{\partial\Omega}$ .

#### Proof.

By the standard interior regularity (see [ZZ20, Theorem 2.2]), $\partial\Omega\cap U\cap\mathrm{Int}(N)$ is a smooth embedded stable $h$ -PMC hypersurface. Suppose for contradiction that a component $\Sigma$ of $\partial\Omega\cap U$ touches $\partial N\cap U$ .

We first claim that $\Sigma$ must be identically $\partial N\cap U$ . Suppose otherwise, so $\Sigma$ contains a point in $\mathrm{Int}(N)\cap U$ . By Theorem 4.1, we can find a ball $B\subset\partial N$ and a relatively open set $W\subset U$ so that (in normal Fermi coordinates over $\partial N$ ) $\Sigma\cap W$ is the graph of a $C^{1,\alpha}$ function $u$ on $\overline{B}$ satisfying $u\mid_{\mathrm{Int}(B)}>0$ , $u(y)=0$ for some $y\in\partial B$ , and $\nabla u(y)=0$ . Since $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ , we have (depending on whether $\partial N\cap W\subset P_{+}$ or $\partial N\cap W\subset P_{-}$ ) that $\overline{\Omega}\cap W$ is the sublevel graph of $u$ (respectively the suplevel graph of $u$ ). We now arrive at a contradiction by the interior regularity, the Hopf lemma, and the assumption that $\partial N$ is a barrier. So we conclude that $\Sigma$ is identically $\partial N\cap U$ , and the rest of $\partial\Omega\cap U$ lies in $U\cap\mathrm{Int}(N)$ by embeddedness.

Since $\partial N$ is a barrier and $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ minimizes $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ in $U$ , the first variation of $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ for any inward pointing vector field with small compact support in $U$ gives a contradiction, so we conclude that $\partial\Omega\cap U\subset\mathrm{Int}(N)$ . ∎

#### 4.2. Unique continuation

Let $\tilde{\mathcal{S}}\subset C^{\infty}(\tilde{N})$ consist of smooth Morse functions $\tilde{h}\in C^{\infty}(\tilde{N})$ so that $\tilde{h}^{-1}(0)$ is a smooth closed hypersurface whose mean curvature vanishes to at most finite order. By [ZZ20, Proposition 0.2], $\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ is an open and dense subset of $C^{\infty}(\tilde{N})$ .

Let $\mathcal{S}\subset C^{\infty}(N)$ consist of those $h\in C^{\infty}(N)$ so that there is some $\tilde{h}\in\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ with $\tilde{h}\mid_{N}=h$ .

#### Proposition 4.3.

$\mathcal{S}$ is a dense subset of $C^{\infty}(N)$ .

#### Proof.

Take $h\in C^{\infty}(N)$ . Let $\tilde{h}$ be any extension of $h$ to $\tilde{N}$ . By the density of $\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ , there is a sequence $\{\tilde{h}_{i}\}_{i}\subset\tilde{\mathcal{S}}$ converging smoothly to $\tilde{h}$ . By definition, $\{\tilde{h}_{i}\mid_{N}\}\subset\mathcal{S}$ converges smoothly to $\tilde{h}\mid_{N}=h$ , as desired. ∎

By [ZZ20, Theorem 3.11], $h$ -PMC hypersurfaces for functions $h\in\mathcal{S}$ satisfy a unique continuation property required for the proof of regularity of almost minimizers in min-max.

### 5. Min-max with barrier

In this section, we prove the following theorem.

#### Theorem 5.1.

Suppose $h\in\mathcal{S}$ and $\partial N$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+},P_{-})$ . Assume

$$ \mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)>\sup_{z\in Z}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(z)). $$

Then there is $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ so that $\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)=\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)$ and $\Sigma=\partial\Omega$ is a smooth, closed, almost embedded hypersurface contained in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ satisfying $H_{\Sigma,\Omega}=h\mid_{\Sigma}$ .

#### 5.1. Nontriviality

Here we show that $\partial^{*}\Omega\neq\varnothing$ . If $\partial^{*}\Omega=\varnothing$ , then $\Omega\in\{\varnothing,\tilde{N}\}$ 77 7 This scenario is only possible if at least one of $E_{-}$ or $E_{+}$ is empty.. By the isoperimetric inequality in $\tilde{N}$ (see [ZZ20, Theorem 2.3]), $\varnothing$ and $\tilde{N}$ are strict minimizers for $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ in a small flat neighborhood, so any nontrivial min-max $h$ -width cannot equal $\mathcal{A}^{h}(\varnothing)$ nor $\mathcal{A}^{h}(\tilde{N})$ (as $X$ is connected and $Z$ is nonempty).

#### 5.2. Pull-tight

Let $c=\sup_{N}|h|$ and $L=2(\mathbf{L}^{h}+c\mathrm{Vol}(\tilde{N}))$ . Let

$$ A^{L}=\{V\in\mathcal{V}_{n}(N)\mid\|V\|(N)\leq L\} $$

and

$$ \displaystyle A_{\infty} \displaystyle=\{V\in A^{L}\mid V\ \text{has}\ c\text{-bounded constrained first variation in}\ N\}\cup\{|\partial^{*}\Phi_{0}(z)|\mid z\in Z\}. $$

We follow the construction of [Zho20, §1.2], [ZZ20, §5], and [ZZ19, §4] for a map to the space of vector fields $\mathcal{D}:A^{L}\to\mathcal{X}_{\text{cpt}}(N)$ . By the definition of $A_{\infty}$ , if $V\in A^{L}$ satisfies $2^{-j}\leq\mathbf{F}(V,A_{\infty})\leq 2^{-j+1}$ , then we can find $X_{V}\in\mathcal{X}_{\text{cpt}}^{+}(N)$ so that

$$ \|X_{V}\|_{C^{1}}\leq 1,\ \ \delta V(X_{V})+c\int_{N}|X_{V}|\ d\|V\|\leq-c_{j}<0, $$

where $c_{j}>0$ does not depend on $V$ . Since the map to vector fields in [ZZ19, §4.2] is constructed using linear combinations of the vector fields $X_{V}$ for some $V$ , the identical construction actually gives $\mathcal{D}:A^{L}\to\mathcal{X}_{\text{cpt}}^{+}(N)$ . Hence, we can use $\mathcal{D}$ to construct the desired tightening map using flows as in [ZZ19, §4.3, §4.4] (the flows stay in $N$ by construction).

To summarize, we obtain an $\mathbf{F}$ -continuous map

$$ \mathcal{PT}:[0,1]\times\{\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)\mid|\partial^{*}\Omega|\in A^{L}\}\to\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N) $$

satisfying

- • $\mathcal{PT}(0,\Omega)=\Omega$ for all $\Omega$ ,

- • $\mathcal{PT}(t,\Omega)=\Omega$ for all $t\in[0,1]$ if $|\partial^{*}\Omega|\in A_{\infty}$ ,

- • there is a continuous function $L:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ with $L(0)=0$ and $L(t)>0$ for $t>0$ so that

$$ \mathcal{A}^{h}(\mathcal{PT}(1,\Omega))-\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)\leq-L(\mathbf{F}(|\partial^{*}\Omega|,A_{\infty})). $$

#### Lemma 5.2 (Pull-tight).

Let $\{\Phi^{*}_{i}\}_{i}\subset\Pi$ be a minimizing sequence. Then there is another minimizing sequence $\{\Phi_{i}\}_{i}\subset\Pi$ so that $\mathbf{C}(\{\Phi_{i}\})\subset\mathbf{C}(\{\Phi_{i}^{*}\})\cap A_{\infty}$ .

#### Proof.

The proof of [Zho20, Lemma 1.8] applies. ∎

#### 5.3. Existence of almost minimizers

We make the same definition of $h$ -almost minimizing as in [ZZ20, Definition 6.1].

#### Definition 5.3.

For $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ and $U\subset N$ relatively open, we define $\mathscr{A}^{h}(U;\varepsilon,\delta)$ to be the set of $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ such that if $\Omega=\Omega_{0},\ \Omega_{1},\ldots,\Omega_{m}\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ satisfies

- • $\Omega_{i}\triangle\Omega\subset U$ ,

- • $\mathcal{F}([\partial^{*}\Omega_{i}]-[\partial^{*}\Omega_{i+1}])\leq\delta$ ,

- • $\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega_{i})\leq\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)+\delta$ ,

then $\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega_{m})\geq\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)-\varepsilon$ .

We say that $V\in\mathcal{V}_{n}(N)$ is $h$ -almost minimizing in $U$ if there are $\varepsilon_{i},\delta_{i}\to 0$ and $\Omega_{i}\in\mathscr{A}^{h}(U;\varepsilon_{i},\delta_{i})$ such that $|\partial^{*}\Omega_{i}|\rightharpoonup V$ .

#### Proposition 5.4.

If $V\in\mathcal{V}_{n}(N)$ is $h$ -almost minimizing in $U$ , then $V$ has $c$ -bounded constrained first variation in $U$ for $c=\sup|h|$ .

#### Proof.

The same proof as [ZZ19, Lemma 5.2] applies. ∎

#### Definition 5.5.

We say $V\in\mathcal{V}_{n}(N)$ is $h$ -almost minimizing in small annuli if for any $p\in N$ , there exists $r_{\text{am}}(p)>0$ such that $V$ is $h$ -almost minimizing in $A_{s,r}^{N}(p)$ for all $0<s<r\leq r_{\text{am}}(p)$ .

#### Theorem 5.6.

For every pulled-tight minimizing sequence $\{\Phi_{i}\}$ in $\Pi$ , there is some $V\in\mathbf{C}(\{\Phi_{i}\})$ that has $c$ -bounded constrained first variation in $N$ and is $h$ -almost minimizing in small annuli.

#### Proof.

The proof follows from the combinatorial construction of [Pit81, 4.9, 4.10] (see [Zho20, Theorem 1.16]) and the discretization and interpolation constructions of [Zho20, §1.3]. That $V$ has $c$ -bounded constrained first variation in $N$ follows from the same argument as the final paragraph of the proof of [Zho20, Theorem 1.7]. ∎

#### 5.4. Regularity of almost minimizers

The interior regularity theory of [ZZ20, Theorem 7.1] is local, and therefore applies to $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ . Hence, we only need to deal with the boundary. Throughout this subsection, we exploit the fact that $c$ -bounded contrained first variation in $N$ implies $C$ -bounded first variation in $\tilde{N}$ for some $C(N,c)$ (by Lemma 2.3).

We first recall the construction of replacements for $h$ -almost minimizing varifolds.

#### Lemma 5.7 (Constrained minimization).

Let $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ and $U\subset N$ relatively open. Take $\Omega\in\mathscr{A}^{h}(U;\varepsilon,\delta)$ . Fix a relatively compact subset $K\subset U$ . Let $\mathcal{C}_{\Omega}$ be the set of $\Lambda\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ such that there is a sequence $\Omega=\Omega_{0},\ \Omega_{1},\ldots,\Omega_{m}=\Lambda$ in $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ satisfying

- • $\Omega_{i}\triangle\Omega\subset K$ ,

- • $\mathcal{F}([\partial^{*}\Omega_{i}]-[\partial^{*}\Omega_{i+1}])\leq\delta$ ,

- • $\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega_{i})\leq\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)+\delta$ .

Then there exists $\Omega^{*}\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ such that

- (1) $\Omega^{*}\in\mathcal{C}_{\Omega}$ and

$$ \mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega^{*})=\inf\{\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Lambda)\mid\Lambda\in\mathcal{C}_{\Omega}\}, $$

- (2) $\Omega^{*}$ is locally minimizing for $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ in $\mathrm{int}_{\mathrm{rel}}(K)$ ,

- (3) $\Omega^{*}\in\mathscr{A}^{h}(U;\varepsilon,\delta)$ .

#### Proof.

The proof follows from the proof of [ZZ20, Lemma 6.7], [ZZ19, Lemma 5.7]. ∎

#### Remark 5.8.

If $\partial N$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+},P_{-})$ , Lemma 5.7 (1) and (2) combined with Corollary 4.2 imply that $\partial^{*}\Omega^{*}\cap\mathrm{int}_{\mathrm{rel}}(K)=\partial\Omega^{*}\cap\mathrm{int}_{\mathrm{rel}}(K)$ is an $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -stable smooth embedded $h$ -PMC hypersurface contained in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ .

#### Proposition 5.9 (Existence of replacements).

Let $V\in\mathcal{V}_{n}(N)$ be $h$ -almost minimizing in a relatively open set $U\subset N$ . Let $K\subset U$ be a compact subset. Then there exists $V^{*}\in\mathcal{V}_{n}(N)$ , called an $h$ -replacement for $V$ in $K$ , so that

- (1) $V\llcorner(N\setminus K)=V^{*}\llcorner(N\setminus K)$ ,

- (2) $-c\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(K)\leq\|V\|(N)-\|V^{*}\|(N)\leq c\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(K)$ ,

- (3) $V^{*}$ is $h$ -almost minimizing in $U$ ,

- (4) there are $\Omega_{i}^{*}\in\mathscr{A}^{h}(U;\varepsilon_{i},\delta_{i})$ with $\varepsilon_{i},\delta_{i}\to 0$ so that $\Omega_{i}^{*}$ locally minimizes $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ in $\mathrm{int}_{\mathrm{rel}}(K)$ and $|\partial^{*}\Omega_{i}^{*}|\rightharpoonup V^{*}$ ,

- (5) if $V$ has $c$ -bounded constrained first variation in $N$ , then so does $V^{*}$ .

#### Proof.

The proof follows [ZZ20, Proposition 6.8], [ZZ19, Proposition 5.8]. ∎

#### Proposition 5.10 (Regularity of replacements).

Under the same hypotheses as Proposition 5.9, if $\partial N$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+},P_{-})$ , then $V^{*}\llcorner\mathrm{int}_{\mathrm{rel}}(K)=|\Sigma|$ for $\Sigma$ a smooth almost embedded stable $h$ -PMC hypersurface in $\mathrm{int}_{\mathrm{rel}}(K)\cap\mathrm{Int}(N)$ .

#### Proof.

As in [ZZ20, Proposition 6.9], [ZZ19, Proposition 5.9], the result follows from the regularity of local minimizers in Corollary 4.2 (which applies because we assumed that $\partial N$ is a barrier) and the compactness theory for stable $h$ -PMC hypersurfaces with uniformly bounded area (see [ZZ20, Theorem 3.6]). The fact that the limit lies in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ follows from the fact that $\partial N$ is a barrier and the maximum principle. ∎

#### Proposition 5.11 (Tangent cones are planar).

Suppose $\partial N$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+},P_{-})$ . Suppose $V\in\mathcal{V}_{n}(N)$ has $c$ -bounded constrained first variation in $N$ and is $h$ -almost minimizing in a relatively open set $U\subset N$ . For any $y\in\partial N\cap U\cap\mathrm{spt}\|V\|$ and $C\in\mathrm{VarTan}(V,y)$ ,

$$ C=m|T_{y}\partial N| $$

for some $m\in\mathbb{N}$ .

#### Proof.

The arguments of [ZZ20, Proposition 6.10, 6.11], [ZZ19, Proposition 5.10, 5.11] apply to guarantee that any tangent cone is an integer multiple of a hyperplane in $T_{y}\tilde{N}$ . Since $\mathrm{spt}\|V\|\subset N$ , this hyperplane must be contained in the closed halfspace $\overline{T_{y}^{+}N}$ and containing the origin, and therefore must equal $T_{y}\partial N$ . ∎

We can now use the properties of replacements to exclude boundary touching when we choose $h\in\mathcal{S}$ .

#### Proposition 5.12 (Interior for almost minimizing).

Suppose $\partial N$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+},P_{-})$ and $h\in\mathcal{S}$ . Suppose $V\in\mathcal{V}_{n}(N)$ has $c$ -bounded constrained first variation in $N$ and is $h$ -almost minimizing in a relatively open set $U\subset N$ . Then $\mathrm{spt}\|V\|\cap U\cap\partial N=\varnothing$ .

#### Proof.

Suppose for contradiction that $y\in U\cap\partial N\cap\mathrm{spt}\|V\|$ . Let $x\in U\cap\partial N$ with $d(x,y)=d$ small so that $\partial B_{d}(x)$ intersects $\partial N$ transversally and $B_{2d}(x)\cap N\subset U$ .

Let $V^{\prime}$ be an $h$ -replacement for $V$ in $\overline{B_{d}^{N}(x)}$ . By Proposition 5.11 and the assumption of transversality, $y\in\mathrm{spt}\|V^{\prime}\|$ . Since $V^{\prime}$ is almost minimizing, Proposition 5.11 implies that every tangent cone to $V^{\prime}$ at $y$ is an integer multiple of $T_{y}\partial N$ . Hence, any varifold $V^{*}$ that agrees with $V^{\prime}$ on $A_{d/2,d}^{N}(x)$ has $y\in\mathrm{spt}\|V^{*}\|$ .

Let $V^{\prime\prime}$ be an $h$ -replacement for $V^{\prime}$ in $\overline{A_{d/2,3d/2}^{N}(x)}$ . By Proposition 5.10,

$$ \mathrm{spt}\|V^{\prime\prime}\|\cap A_{d/2,3d/2}^{N}(x)\cap\partial N=\varnothing, $$

so $y\notin\mathrm{spt}\|V^{\prime\prime}\|$ . However, by the gluing and unique continuation arguments from the proof of [ZZ20, Theorem 7.1] (which apply because they are local and the gluing happens in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ , and we assumed $h\in\mathcal{S}$ ), $V^{\prime\prime}$ agrees with $V^{\prime}$ on $A_{d/2,d}^{N}(x)$ , so $y\in\mathrm{spt}\|V^{\prime\prime}\|$ by the above paragraph. Hence, we reach a contradiction. ∎

We now use a removable singularities result to deduce the same conclusion for varifolds that are $h$ -almost minimizing in annuli.

#### Theorem 5.13.

Suppose $\partial N$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+},P_{-})$ and $h\in\mathcal{S}$ . Suppose $V\in\mathcal{V}_{n}(N)$ has $c$ -bounded constrained first variation in $N$ and is $h$ -almost minimizing in small annuli. Then $V$ is the varifold of a smooth almost embedded $h$ -PMC hypersurface in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ .

#### Proof.

By Proposition 5.12, $\mathrm{spt}\|V\|\cap\partial N$ consists of finitely many isolated points. By removable singularities (see [ZZ20, Proof of Theorem 7.1, Step 4]), $V$ is the varifold of a smooth almost embedded $h$ -PMC hypersurface, with finitely many isolated points touching $\partial N$ tangentially. Since $\partial N$ is a barrier, the standard maximum principle implies $\mathrm{spt}\|V\|\cap\partial N=\varnothing$ . ∎

Now that we know that $V$ avoids the boundary, Theorem 5.1 follows as in [ZZ20].

### 6. Min-max with barrier in generic metrics

We use special results applicable to a generic set of metrics and prescribing functions to upgrade the conclusions of Theorem 5.1.

#### 6.1. Good pairs

Let $(N,\partial N)$ be a compact manifold with smooth boundary. We say a pair $(g,h)$ , where $g$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $N$ and $h\in C^{\infty}(N)$ , is a good pair, if

- • $h\in\mathcal{S}(g)$ 88 8 Here we include explicitly in the notation the dependence of $\mathcal{S}$ on the metric, since we consider varying metrics on $N$ . as defined in §4.2

- • every closed two-sided almost embedded $h$ -PMC hypersurface in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ is embedded and $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -nondegenerate.

The following result is a consequence of [Zho20, Lemma 3.5], building on [ZZ20, Proposition 0.2] and [Whi19, Theorems 34 and 35].

#### Theorem 6.1.

Let $N$ be a compact manifold with smooth boundary. The set of good pairs is $C^{\infty}$ dense.

#### Proof.

Let $(g,h)$ be a Riemannian metric and smooth function on $N$ . Let $(\tilde{g},\tilde{h})$ be any extension of $g$ and $h$ to $\tilde{N}$ . By [Zho20, Lemma 3.5], there is a sequence of good pairs $(\tilde{g}_{i},\tilde{h}_{i})$ for $\tilde{N}$ in the sense of [Zho20, §3.3] converging smoothly to $(\tilde{g},\tilde{h})$ . Since the restriction to $N$ of a good pair on $\tilde{N}$ is a good pair on $N$ by definition, $(\tilde{g}_{i}\mid_{N},\tilde{h}_{i}\mid_{N})$ is a sequence of good pairs converging smoothly to $(g,h)$ , as desired. ∎

#### 6.2. Minimality for strict stability

We show, based on the arguments of [IM18], that a strictly $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -stable hypersurface minimizes $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ in a small flat neighborhood.

#### Theorem 6.2.

Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth closed Riemannian manifold. Let $\Sigma=\partial\Omega$ be a smooth closed embedded $h$ -PMC hypersurface which is strictly $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -stable. Then there exists $\varepsilon>0$ (depending on $\Omega$ and $M$ ) so that

$$ \mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega^{\prime})>\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega) $$

for all $\Omega^{\prime}\in\mathcal{C}(M)$ with $0<\mathcal{F}([\partial\Omega]-[\partial^{*}\Omega^{\prime}])<\varepsilon$ .

#### Proof.

We follow the proof of [IM18, Proposition 3.1], but we take extra care because $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ is not necessarily an elliptic parametric functional in the sense of [IM18, §2.2] on all of $M$ .

As observed on [Whi94, Page 205], $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ on a small tubular neighborhood of $\Sigma$ is an elliptic parametric functional in the sense of [Whi94, §1] and [IM18, §2.2], so [Whi94, Theorem 2] applies.

We observe that upper bounds on $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ imply upper bounds on area (since $h$ is smooth and $M$ is compact), so the arguments of [IM18] requiring the compactness theory for bounded area apply. Moreover, since flat convergence implies $L^{1}$ convergence of the indicator functions of the finite perimeter sets (as noted in §3.1), $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ is lower semi-continuous with respect to $\mathcal{F}$ -convergence.

The arguments of [IM18, §3.2] apply verbatim, with the additional observation that [IM18, Lemma 3.5] for $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ follows directly from [IM18, Lemma 3.5] for area combined with [IM18, Lemma 3.4] (to handle the integral of $h$ terms).

The arguments of [IM18, §3.3] preceding [IM18, Lemma 3.8] apply to prove [IM18, (3.7)] with $F=\mathcal{A}^{h}$ . Moving the integral of $h$ terms to the right hand side (where we write $\Lambda$ to be the integral $(n+1)$ -current supported in $B_{r}(x_{0})$ with $\partial\Lambda=X$ ), we get

$$ \mathbf{M}(R_{\delta,\lambda})\leq\mathbf{M}(R_{\delta,\lambda}+X)+\lambda\mathcal{F}(X)+c\mathbf{M}(\Lambda). $$

We can now apply [IM18, Lemma 3.4] (since we can assume $\mathcal{F}(X)\leq\varepsilon_{0}$ for the almost minimizing condition) to deduce

$$ \mathbf{M}(R_{\delta,\lambda})\leq\mathbf{M}(R_{\delta,\lambda}+X)+(\lambda+c)\mathcal{F}(X). $$

We can now apply [IM18, Lemma 3.8] to conclude that $R_{\delta,\lambda}$ is almost minimizing for mass. Hence, we can apply [IM18, Lemma 3.10] and conclude. ∎

#### 6.3. Generic min-max theorem

The following result upgrades the conclusions of Theorem 5.1 for good pairs.

#### Theorem 6.3.

Suppose $(g,h)$ is a good pair and $\partial N$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+},P_{-})$ . Assume

$$ \mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)>\sup_{z\in Z}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(z)). $$

Then there is $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ so that $\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)=\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)$ and $\Sigma=\partial\Omega$ is a smooth, closed, embedded hypersurface contained in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ satisfying $H_{\Sigma,\Omega}=h\mid_{\Sigma}$ and $1\leq\mathrm{index}_{\mathcal{A}^{h}}(\Sigma)\leq k$ .

#### Proof.

The only new conclusions beyond Theorem 5.1 are embeddedness and the index bounds.

Embeddedness follows immediately from the assumption the $(g,h)$ is a good pair.

Since $\partial\Omega$ is embedded and contained in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ , the index upper bound of [Zho20, Theorem 3.6] (which is a local deformation argument) applies.

The index lower bound follows from Theorem 6.2. Indeed, if $\Sigma$ was $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -stable, then $\Sigma$ would be strictly $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -stable since $(g,h)$ is a good pair. Then by Theorem 6.2, $\Omega$ strictly minimizes $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ in a flat neighborhood, so any nontrivial min-max $h$ -width cannot equal $\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)$ (as $X$ is connected and $Z$ is nonempty). ∎

#### 6.4. Corollaries of generic min-max

We record two consequence of Theorem 6.3 combined with the compactness theory for $h$ -PMC hypersurfaces with uniformly bounded area and index (see [Zho20, Theorem 2.8]).

The first corollary is that the index upper bound applies for metrics $g$ that are not bumpy.

#### Corollary 6.4.

Suppose $h\in\mathcal{S}$ and $\partial N$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+},P_{-})$ . Assume

$$ \mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)>\sup_{z\in Z}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(z)). $$

Then there is $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ so that $\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)=\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)$ and $\Sigma=\partial\Omega$ is a smooth, closed, almost embedded hypersurface contained in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ satisfying $H_{\Sigma,\Omega}=h\mid_{\Sigma}$ and $\mathrm{index}_{\mathcal{A}^{h}}(\Sigma)\leq k$ .

The second corollary is that existence (and the index upper bound) applies for $g$ that are not bumpy and $h$ that are not in $\mathcal{S}$ .

#### Corollary 6.5.

Suppose $\partial N$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+},P_{-})$ . Assume

$$ \mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)>\sup_{z\in Z}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(z)). $$

Then there is a smooth, closed, two-sided, almost embedded $h$ -PMC hypersurface $\Sigma$ contained in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ satisfying $\mathcal{H}^{n}(\Sigma)\leq\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)+\int_{\{h>0\}}h$ and $\mathrm{index}_{\mathcal{A}^{h}}(\Sigma)\leq k$ .

### 7. Localization in compact manifolds with barrier

Using our generic min-max result from Theorem 6.3, we develop a cutting argument to localize min-max hypersurfaces.

#### 7.1. Setup

We make a few specialized definitions related to the min-max setup considered above. See Figure 3 for an illustration.

*Figure 3. Span, unspanned halves, and localizer.*

#### Definition 7.1 (Span).

The span of $\Phi_{0}$ is

$$ \mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0})=\overline{\bigcup_{x\in X}\partial^{*}\Phi_{0}(x)}. $$

#### Definition 7.2 (Unspanned halves).

For any $x_{0}\in X$ 99 9 Recall that we assume (without loss of generality) that $\partial\Phi_{0}(x)=\overline{\partial^{*}\Phi_{0}(x)}$ for all $x\in X$ ., we define the positive and negative unspanned halves by

$$ I_{+}(\Phi_{0})=(N\cap\mathrm{Int}(\Phi_{0}(x_{0})))\setminus\mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0})\ \ \text{and}\ \ I_{-}(\Phi_{0})=(N\setminus\overline{\Phi_{0}(x_{0})})\setminus\mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0}). $$

Note that $I_{\pm}(\Phi_{0})$ are well-defined: for any $x\in X$ we have

$$ I_{+}(\Phi_{0})\subset\mathrm{Int}(\Phi_{0}(x))\ \ \text{and}\ \ I_{-}(\Phi_{0})\cap\overline{\Phi_{0}(x)}=\varnothing. $$

#### Definition 7.3 (Localizer).

The localizer of $\Phi_{0}$ and $h$ is

$$ \mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)=\mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0})\cup(\overline{I_{+}(\Phi_{0})}\cap\overline{\{h<0\}})\cup(\overline{I_{-}(\Phi_{0})}\cap\overline{\{h>0\}}). $$

#### 7.2. Subdomains

Here we discuss how to restrict the min-max setup to special subdomains of the original compact manifold with boundary.

Let $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ be an open set with smooth boundary in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ satisfying $\partial\Omega\cap\mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0})=\varnothing$ .

*Figure 4. Schematic for the construction of $N^{\prime}$ when $\mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0})\subset\Omega$ .*

We consider two possibilities.

- • $\mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0})\subset\Omega$ . Consider the subdomain $N^{\prime}=N\cap\overline{\Omega}$ . Then $\partial N^{\prime}=P_{+}\sqcup\partial\Omega$ . We define $E_{+}^{\prime}$ to be the union of $E_{+}$ and all components of $\tilde{N}\setminus N^{\prime}$ in $I_{+}$ . $E_{-}^{\prime}$ is defined to be the union of the remaining components of $\tilde{N}\setminus N^{\prime}$ . See Figure 4.

- • $\mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0})\cap\overline{\Omega}=\varnothing$ . Consider the subdomain $N^{\prime}=N\setminus\Omega$ . Then $\partial N^{\prime}=P_{-}\sqcup\partial\Omega$ . We define $E_{-}^{\prime}$ to be the union of $E_{-}$ and all components of $\tilde{N}\setminus N^{\prime}$ in $I_{-}$ . $E_{+}^{\prime}$ is defined to be the union of the remaining components of $\tilde{N}\setminus N^{\prime}$ . See Figure 5.

We record a few observations that apply in both cases.

- • $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+}^{\prime},E_{-}^{\prime}}(N^{\prime})\subset\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ . Hence, $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ (as defined on $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ ) is well-defined on $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+}^{\prime},E_{-}^{\prime}}(N^{\prime})$ .

- • By construction, the image of $\Phi_{0}$ lies in $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+}^{\prime},E_{-}^{\prime}}(N^{\prime})$ . Let $\Pi(N^{\prime})$ denote the $(X,Z)$ -homotopy class of $\Phi_{0}$ for maps to $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+}^{\prime},E_{-}^{\prime}}(N^{\prime})$ , which satisfies $\Pi\supset\Pi(N^{\prime})$ by definition.

- • Let $\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi(N^{\prime}))$ denote the $h$ -width of $\Pi(N^{\prime})$ . Then $\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi(N^{\prime}))\geq\mathbf{L}^{h}(N)$ .

*Figure 5. Schematic for the construction of $N^{\prime}$ when $\mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0})\cap\overline{\Omega}=\varnothing$ .*

#### 7.3. Neighborhood cutting

We use the formula for the derivative of mean curvature along a smooth variation to find good hypersurfaces near unstable and strictly stable $h$ -PMC hypersurfaces along which we will cut our manifold.

#### Lemma 7.4.

Let $(N,\partial N,g)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary and $h\in C^{\infty}(N)$ . Suppose $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ has smooth closed embedded boundary contained in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ . Suppose $\Sigma$ is a connected component of $\partial\Omega$ satisfying $H_{\Sigma,\Omega}=h\mid_{\Sigma}$ and $\Sigma$ is $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -unstable. Then for any $\varepsilon>0$ , there are sets $\Omega_{-}\subset\Omega$ and $\Omega_{+}\supset\Omega$ satisfying

- • $\Sigma\cap\Omega_{-}=\varnothing$ and $\Sigma\subset\Omega_{+}$ ,

- • $\Omega\triangle\Omega_{\pm}\subset B_{\varepsilon}(\Sigma)$ ,

- • $\Sigma_{\pm}=(\partial\Omega_{\pm})\cap B_{\varepsilon}(\Sigma)$ are smooth closed embedded hypersurfaces contained in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ ,

- • $H_{\Sigma_{-},\Omega_{-}}>h\mid_{\Sigma_{-}}$ ,

- • $H_{\Sigma_{+},\Omega_{+}}<h\mid_{\Sigma_{+}}$ .

#### Proof.

Let $\nu$ denote the unit normal vector field along $\Sigma$ pointing out of $\Omega$ . Since $\Sigma=\partial\Omega$ is $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -unstable, there is a negative number $\lambda<0$ and a smooth positive function $\varphi\in C^{\infty}(\Sigma)$ so that

$$ -\Delta_{\Sigma}\varphi-(|A_{\Sigma}|^{2}+\mathrm{Ric}(\nu,\nu))\varphi=(\partial_{\nu}h)\varphi+\lambda\varphi<(\partial_{\nu}h)\varphi. $$

Consider a variation of $\Sigma$ given by $\varphi\nu$ (namely, extend $\varphi\nu$ to a vector field supported in a neighborhood of $\Sigma$ , then apply the flow diffeomorphisms generated by this vector field to $\Sigma$ and $\Omega$ ). Since $\varphi$ is positive and $\Sigma$ is closed and embedded, we obtain a foliation $\{\Sigma_{t}=\partial\Omega_{t}\}_{t\in(-\delta,\delta)}$ of a neighborhood of $\Sigma$ for some small $\delta>0$ , where $\Sigma_{0}=\Sigma$ and $\Omega_{0}=\Omega$ .

Since the derivative of the mean curvature along this foliation at $t=0$ is given by the left hand side of (7.1) and the derivative of $h$ along this foliation at $t=0$ is given by the right hand side of (7.1), we find that for all $\eta>0$ sufficiently small

$$ H_{\Sigma_{-\eta},\Omega_{-\eta}}>h\mid_{\Sigma_{-\eta}}\ ,\ \ H_{\Sigma_{\eta},\Omega_{\eta}}<h\mid_{\Sigma_{\eta}}. $$

We can now take $\Omega_{\pm}=\Omega_{\pm\eta}$ for $\eta>0$ chosen sufficiently small depending on $\varepsilon$ . ∎

#### Lemma 7.5.

Let $(N,\partial N,g)$ be a compact Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary and $h\in C^{\infty}(N)$ . Suppose $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ has smooth closed embedded boundary contained in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ . Suppose $\Sigma$ is a connected component of $\partial\Omega$ satisfying $H_{\Sigma,\Omega}=h\mid_{\Sigma}$ and $\Sigma$ is strictly $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -stable. Then for any $\varepsilon>0$ , there are sets $\Omega_{-}\subset\Omega$ and $\Omega_{+}\supset\Omega$ satisfying

- • $\Sigma\cap\Omega_{-}=\varnothing$ and $\Sigma\subset\Omega_{+}$ ,

- • $\Omega\triangle\Omega_{\pm}\subset B_{\varepsilon}(\Sigma)$ ,

- • $\Sigma_{\pm}=(\partial\Omega_{\pm})\cap B_{\varepsilon}(\Sigma)$ are smooth closed embedded hypersurfaces contained in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ ,

- • $H_{\Sigma_{-},\Omega_{-}}<h\mid_{\Sigma_{-}}$ ,

- • $H_{\Sigma_{+},\Omega_{+}}>h\mid_{\Sigma_{+}}$ .

#### Proof.

The proof is identical to Lemma 7.4, where we flip the direction of the inequality (7.1) due to strict stability. ∎

#### 7.4. Localized min-max theorem with barrier

We are now equipped to prove a localized version of Theorem 5.1.

#### Theorem 7.6.

Suppose $\partial N$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+},P_{-})$ . Assume

$$ \mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)>\sup_{z\in Z}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(z)). $$

Then there is a smooth, closed, two-sided, almost embedded $h$ -PMC hypersurface $\Sigma$ contained in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ satisfying

- • $\mathcal{H}^{n}(\Sigma)\leq\sup_{x\in X}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(x))+\int_{\{h>0\}}h$ ,

- • $\mathrm{index}_{\mathcal{A}^{h}}(\Sigma)\leq k$ ,

- • $\Sigma\cap\mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)\neq\varnothing$ .

#### Proof.

We give the proof when $(g,h)$ is a good pair satisfying

$$ h\mid_{I_{+}(\Phi_{0})\setminus\mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)}>0\ \ \text{and}\ \ h\mid_{I_{-}(\Phi_{0})\setminus\mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)}<0. $$

By Theorem 6.1 and [Zho20, Theorem 2.8], the general conclusion follows by approximation1010 10 To ensure $h$ has the correct sign on the respective sets, we can first add to $h$ the function $\varepsilon\eta$ for $\varepsilon>0$ small and $\eta\in C^{\infty}(N)$ any smooth function satisfying $\eta\mid_{\overline{I}_{+}(\Phi_{0})}>0$ and $\eta\mid_{\overline{I}_{-}(\Phi_{0})}<0$ , and then take $\varepsilon\to 0$ ..

By Theorem 6.3, there is $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ so that $\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)=\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)$ and $\Sigma=\partial\Omega$ is a smooth, closed, embedded, $h$ -PMC hypersurface contained in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ , satisfying $1\leq\mathrm{index}_{\mathcal{A}^{h}}(\Sigma)\leq k$ .

If $\Sigma\cap\mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)\neq\varnothing$ , then we are done.

First, suppose that $\mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)\subset\Omega$ . We modify $\Omega$ in a small neighborhood of $\Sigma$ in the following way. Let $\Sigma^{*}$ be a component of $\Sigma$ , which (by bumpiness) is either unstable or strictly stable for $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ .

- (1) If $\Sigma^{*}\subset I_{+}$ , then $h\mid_{\Sigma^{*}}>0$ . In this case, we modify $\Omega$ near $\Sigma^{*}$ by taking $\Omega_{-}$ from Lemma 7.4 or Lemma 7.5, choosing the perturbation small enough so that the modified boundary $\Sigma_{-}$ has $H_{\Sigma_{-},\Omega_{-}}>0$ .

- (2) If $\Sigma^{*}$ is unstable and $\Sigma^{*}\subset I_{-}$ , then we modify $\Omega$ near $\Sigma^{*}$ by taking $\Omega_{-}$ from Lemma 7.4.

- (3) If $\Sigma^{*}$ is strictly stable and $\Sigma^{*}\subset I_{-}$ , then we modify $\Omega$ near $\Sigma^{*}$ by taking $\Omega_{+}$ from Lemma 7.4.

Let $\Omega^{\prime}$ denote the modification of $\Omega$ . We take the subdomain $N^{\prime}=N\cap\overline{\Omega}^{\prime}$ , with the decomposition $E_{\pm}^{\prime}$ given in §7.2. By construction, for $\Sigma^{*}$ in case (1) above, the modified boundary $\Sigma_{-}$ will lie in $P_{+}^{\prime}$ . Then we have

$$ H_{\Sigma_{-},E_{+}^{\prime}}<0<h\mid_{\Sigma_{-}}, $$

so these boundary components satisfy the barrier property. For $\Sigma^{*}$ in cases (2) and (3), the modified boundary will lie in $P_{-}^{\prime}$ . Then the barrier property follows directly from Lemmas 7.4 and 7.5 respectively.

Second, suppose that $\mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)\cap\overline{\Omega}=\varnothing$ . We modify $\Omega$ in a small neighborhood of $\Sigma$ in the following way. Let $\Sigma^{*}$ be a component of $\Sigma$ , which (by bumpiness) is either unstable or strictly stable for $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ .

- (1) If $\Sigma^{*}\subset I_{-}$ , then $h\mid_{\Sigma^{*}}<0$ . In this case, we modify $\Omega$ near $\Sigma^{*}$ by taking $\Omega_{+}$ from Lemma 7.4 or Lemma 7.5, choosing the perturbation small enough so that the modified boundary $\Sigma_{+}$ has $H_{\Sigma_{+},\Omega_{+}}<0$ .

- (2) If $\Sigma^{*}$ is unstable and $\Sigma^{*}\subset I_{+}$ , then we modify $\Omega$ near $\Sigma^{*}$ by taking $\Omega_{+}$ from Lemma 7.4.

- (3) If $\Sigma^{*}$ is strictly stable and $\Sigma^{*}\subset I_{+}$ , then we modify $\Omega$ near $\Sigma^{*}$ by taking $\Omega_{-}$ from Lemma 7.5.

Let $\Omega^{\prime}$ denote the modification of $\Omega$ . We take the subdomain $N^{\prime}=N\setminus\mathrm{Int}(\Omega^{\prime})$ , with the decomposition $E_{\pm}^{\prime}$ given in §7.2. By construction, for $\Sigma^{*}$ in case (1) above, the modified boundary $\Sigma_{+}$ will lie in $P_{-}^{\prime}$ . Then we have

$$ H_{\Sigma_{+},E_{-}^{\prime}}<0<-h\mid_{\Sigma_{-}}, $$

so these boundary components satisfy the barrier property. For $\Sigma^{*}$ in cases (2) and (3), the modified boundary will lie in $P_{+}^{\prime}$ . Then the barrier property follows directly from Lemmas 7.4 and 7.5 respectively.

In both cases, we find a subdomain $N^{\prime}$ with decomposition $E_{\pm}^{\prime}$ so that

- • $\mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0})\subset\mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)\subset N^{\prime}$ ,

- • $\partial N^{\prime}$ is a barrier for $(h,P_{+}^{\prime},P_{-}^{\prime})$ ,

- • the unstable components of $\Sigma$ (of which there is at least one by Theorem 6.3) are not contained in $N^{\prime}$ ,

- • $(g\mid_{N^{\prime}},h\mid_{N^{\prime}})$ is a good pair1111 11 It follows from the definition that the restriction of a good pair to a subdomain is a good pair.,

- • $\sup_{x\in X}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(x))\geq\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi(N^{\prime}))\geq\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)>\sup_{z\in Z}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(z))$ .

Hence, we can re-apply Theorem 6.3 on $N^{\prime}$ , and therefore iterate the above steps. Since each iteration produces a distinct, connected, $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -unstable, smooth, closed, embedded, $h$ -PMC hypersurface $\Sigma^{\prime}$ with

$$ \mathcal{H}^{n}(\Sigma^{\prime})\leq\sup_{x\in X}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(x))+\int_{\{h>0\}}h<\infty $$

and $\mathrm{index}_{\mathcal{A}^{h}}(\Sigma^{\prime})\leq k$ , the iteration must terminate after at most finitely many steps by the bumpiness of the metric (if there were infinitely many such hypersurfaces, [Zho20, Theorem 2.6(iv)] yields a limit embedded $h$ -PMC hypersurface that is degenerate). Hence, at some step of the iteration the output of Theorem 6.3 will satisfy $\Sigma\cap\mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)\neq\varnothing$ . ∎

## Part II Noncompact Manifolds

In this part, we apply the localized min-max result of Theorem 7.6 to develop a min-max theory in noncompact manifolds. We also provide applications of the theory.

### 8. Setup

Let $(M,g)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold of dimension $3\leq n+1\leq 7$ .

#### 8.1. Space of subsets

Let $\Omega_{0}$ be an open set with smooth closed boundary (we emphasize that $\Omega_{0}$ need not be bounded).

Let $\mathcal{C}_{\Omega_{0}}(M)$ be the collection of sets of finite perimeter $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}(M)$ so that $\Omega\triangle\Omega_{0}$ is bounded.

#### 8.2. Functional

Let $h\in C^{\infty}_{\text{loc}}(M)$ . For $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{\Omega_{0}}(M)$ , we define

$$ \mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)=\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)-\int_{\Omega\setminus\Omega_{0}}h+\int_{\Omega_{0}\setminus\Omega}h. $$

By the definition of $\mathcal{C}_{\Omega_{0}}(M)$ , $\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)$ is well-defined for all $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{\Omega_{0}}(M)$ .

#### 8.3. Admissible functions

We let $\mathcal{W}_{\Omega_{0}}\subset C_{\text{loc}}^{\infty}(M)$ denote the set of locally smooth functions $h$ with the property that there is a compact set $K_{h}\subset M$ satisfying

$$ h\mid_{\Omega_{0}\setminus K_{h}}\geq 0\ \ \text{and}\ \ h\mid_{(M\setminus\Omega_{0})\setminus K_{h}}\leq 0. $$

Note that if $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{\Omega_{0}}(M)$ , $h\in\mathcal{W}_{\Omega_{0}}$ , and $\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)\leq\Lambda<\infty$ , then

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega) \displaystyle=\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega)+\int_{\Omega\setminus\Omega_{0}}h-\int_{\Omega_{0}\setminus\Omega}h \displaystyle\leq\Lambda+\int_{(\Omega\setminus\Omega_{0})\cap K_{h}}h-\int_{(\Omega_{0}\setminus\Omega)\cap K_{h}}h \displaystyle\leq\Lambda+\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(K_{h})\sup_{K_{h}}|h|<\infty. $$

Hence, for these functions, uniform $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ bounds imply uniform area bounds.

#### 8.4. Min-max setup

We follow the same definitions as §3.4.

Let $X^{k}$ be a connected cubical complex of dimension $k$ in some $I^{m}=[0,1]^{m}$ . Let $Z\subset X$ be a nonempty cubical subcomplex.

Let $\Phi_{0}:X\to\mathcal{C}_{\Omega_{0}}(M)$ be a continuous map in the $\mathbf{F}$ -topology.

#### Definition 8.1 (Homotopy class).

Let $\Pi$ be the set of all sequences of $\mathbf{F}$ -continuous maps $\{\Phi_{i}:X\to\mathcal{C}_{\Omega_{0}}(M)\}_{i}$ so that there are $\mathcal{F}$ -continuous homotopies $\{\Psi_{i}:[0,1]\times X\to\mathcal{C}_{\Omega_{0}}(M)\}_{i}$ satisfying $\Psi_{i}(0,\cdot)=\Phi_{i}$ , $\Psi_{i}(1,\cdot)=\Phi_{0}$ , and

$$ \limsup_{i\to\infty}\sup\{\mathbf{F}(\Psi_{i}(t,z),\Phi_{0}(z))\mid t\in[0,1],\ z\in Z\}=0. $$

Such a sequence $\{\Phi_{i}\}$ is called an $(X,Z)$ -homotopy sequence of mappings to $\mathcal{C}_{\Omega_{0}}(M)$ , and $\Pi$ is called the $(X,Z)$ -homotopy class of $\Phi_{0}$ .

#### Definition 8.2 (Width).

The $h$ -width of $\Pi$ is

$$ \mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)=\inf_{\{\Phi_{i}\}\in\Pi}\limsup_{i\to\infty}\sup_{x\in X}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{i}(x)). $$

#### Definition 8.3 (Minimizing sequence).

We say $\{\Phi_{i}\}_{i}\in\Pi$ is a minimizing sequence if

$$ \limsup_{i\to\infty}\sup_{x\in X}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{i}(x))=\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi). $$

#### Definition 8.4 (Critical set).

The critical set of a minimizing sequence $\{\Phi_{i}\}_{i}\in\Pi$ is

$$ \mathbf{C}(\{\Phi_{i}\})=\left\{V\in\mathcal{V}_{n}(M)\mid V=\lim_{j\to\infty}|\partial^{*}\Phi_{i_{j}}(x_{j})|,\ \lim_{j\to\infty}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{i_{j}}(x_{j}))=\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Phi)\right\}. $$

### 9. Localization in noncompact manifolds

We use our localized min-max theory in compact manifolds with barriers to deduce a localized min-max theory in noncompact manifolds.

#### 9.1. Setup

We follow the same definitions as §7.1.

#### Definition 9.1 (Span).

The span of $\Phi_{0}$ is

$$ \mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0})=\overline{\bigcup_{x\in X}\partial^{*}\Phi_{0}(x)}. $$

#### Definition 9.2 (Unspanned halves).

For any $x_{0}\in X$ 1212 12 Recall that we can assume (without loss of generality) that $\partial\Phi_{0}(x)=\overline{\partial^{*}\Phi_{0}(x)}$ for all $x\in X$ ., we define the positive and negative unspanned halves by

$$ I_{+}(\Phi_{0})=(M\cap\mathrm{Int}(\Phi_{0}(x_{0})))\setminus\mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0})\ \ \text{and}\ \ I_{-}(\Phi_{0})=(M\setminus\overline{\Phi_{0}(x_{0})})\setminus\mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0}). $$

Note that $I_{\pm}(\Phi_{0})$ are well-defined: for any $x\in X$ we have

$$ I_{+}(\Phi_{0})\subset\mathrm{Int}(\Phi_{0}(x))\ \ \text{and}\ \ I_{-}(\Phi_{0})\cap\overline{\Phi_{0}(x)}=\varnothing. $$

#### Definition 9.3 (Localizer).

The localizer of $\Phi_{0}$ and $h$ is

$$ \mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)=\mathrm{Span}(\Phi_{0})\cup(\overline{I_{+}(\Phi_{0})}\cap\overline{\{h<0\}})\cup(\overline{I_{-}(\Phi_{0})}\cap\overline{\{h>0\}}). $$

#### Remark 9.4.

For $h\in\mathcal{W}_{\Omega_{0}}$ , the localizer $\mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)$ is a compact set.

#### 9.2. Compact subdomains

Here we discuss how to restrict the min-max setup to special compact subdomains of the original complete manifold, where we assume $h\in\mathcal{W}_{\Omega_{0}}$ .

Let $N\subset M$ be a compact subdomain with smooth boundary satisfying $\mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)\subset N$ .

We give $N$ a boundary decomposition as in §3.1 by

$$ P_{+}=\partial N\cap I_{+}(\Phi_{0})\ \ \text{and}\ \ P_{-}=\partial N\cap I_{-}(\Phi_{0}). $$

We also set

$$ F_{+}=I_{+}(\Phi_{0})\setminus N\ \ \text{and}\ \ F_{-}=I_{-}(\Phi_{0})\setminus N. $$

Let $\mathcal{C}_{F_{+},F_{-}}(M)$ be the space of $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{\Omega_{0}}(M)$ satisfying

$$ F_{+}\subset\Omega\ \ \text{and}\ \ \Omega\cap F_{-}=\varnothing. $$

Let $(\tilde{N},\tilde{g})$ be a closed Riemannian manifold of dimension $n+1$ containing $(N,g)$ isometrically, and so that $\tilde{N}\setminus N$ has a decomposition $E_{+}\sqcup E_{-}$ into unions of connected components of $\tilde{N}\setminus N$ satisfying $\partial E_{\pm}=P_{\pm}$ .

We are now in the setting of Part I. We make a few observations.

- • There is a natural $\mathbf{F}$ -homeomorphism from $\mathcal{C}_{F_{+},F_{-}}(M)$ to $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ given by deleting $F_{+}$ from $\Omega$ and adding $E_{+}$ .

- • Using this homeomorphism, $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ as defined in §8.2 is well-defined on $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ . Moreover, this definition of $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ only differs from §3.2 by a fixed constant, which does not affect the theory in Part I (since the difference of $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ between any two sets is unchanged).

- • By construction, the image of $\Phi_{0}$ under this homeomorphism lies in $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ . Let $\Pi(N)$ denote the $(X,Z)$ -homotopy class of $\Phi_{0}$ for maps to $\mathcal{C}_{E_{+},E_{-}}(N)$ , which satisfies $\Pi\supset\Pi(N)$ by definition.

- • Let $\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi(N))$ denote the $h$ -width of $\Pi(N)$ . Then $\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi(N))\geq\mathbf{L}^{h}(N)$ .

#### 9.3. Localized min-max theorem in noncompact manifolds

In this subsection, we prove the main min-max theorem in noncompact manifolds.

#### Theorem 9.5.

Suppose $h\in\mathcal{W}_{\Omega_{0}}$ . Suppose

$$ \mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi)>\sup_{z\in Z}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(z)). $$

Then there is a smooth, complete, almost embedded, $h$ -PMC hypersurface $\Sigma$ in $M$ satisfying

- • $\mathcal{H}^{n}(\Sigma)\leq\sup_{x\in X}\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(x))+\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(K_{h})\sup_{K_{h}}|h|<\infty$ ,

- • $\mathrm{index}_{\mathcal{A}^{h}}(\Sigma)\leq k$ ,

- • $\Sigma\cap\mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)\neq\varnothing$ .

#### Proof.

Let $\{N_{i}\}_{i}$ be a nested compact exhaustion of $M$ with smooth boundary satisfying $\mathrm{Loc}(\Phi_{0},h)\subset N_{1}$ .

Fix any $i$ (henceforth we drop the subscript). We follow the constructions of §9.2 for $N$ , which produces a boundary decomposition $P_{\pm}$ .

We modify $h$ to $\tilde{h}$ near $\partial N$ so that $\tilde{h}\mid_{P_{+}}>H_{P_{+},M\setminus N}$ , $-\tilde{h}\mid_{P_{-}}>H_{P_{-},M\setminus N}$ , and $\int_{\tilde{N}}|h-\tilde{h}|$ is arbitrarily small.

Then $\partial N$ is a barrier for $(\tilde{h},P_{+},P_{-})$ and $\mathbf{L}^{\tilde{h}}(\Pi(N))>\sup_{z\in Z}\mathcal{A}^{\tilde{h}}(\Phi_{0}(z))$ .

We can now apply Theorem 7.6, producing a smooth closed almost embedded $\tilde{h}$ -PMC hypersurface $\Sigma$ in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ satisfying the conclusions of Theorem 7.61313 13 The difference in the area bounds is simply a reflection of the fact that the definition of $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ here differs from the definition of $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ in Part I by a fixed constant..

The theorem follows by taking the limit over the compact exhaustion and applying the compactness theory from [Zho20, Theorem 2.8]. ∎

### 10. Application I: PMC hypersurfaces in Euclidean space

We use the theory developed in Theorem 5.1 (and Corollary 6.5) to provide new answers to Question 1.1.

#### Theorem 10.1.

If $h\in C^{\infty}_{\text{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^{n+1})$ for $3\leq n+1\leq 7$ satisfies

- (1) there is a compact set with smooth boundary $N\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ satisfying $h<H_{\partial N,N}$ ,

- (2) there is an $\mathbf{F}$ -continuous map $\Phi_{0}:[0,1]\to\mathcal{C}_{\varnothing}(\mathbb{R}^{n+1})$ satisfying $\Phi_{0}(t)\subset N$ for all $t$ and

$$ \mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi_{\Phi_{0}}(N))>\max\{\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(0)),\ \mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(1))\}. $$

then there exists a smooth closed almost embedded $h$ -PMC hypersurface contained in $\mathrm{Int}(N)$ with $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -index at most 1.

#### Remark 10.2.

We emphasize that condition (1) is only a 1-sided bounded; $h$ is allowed to be arbitrarily negative.

#### Proof.

Apply Theorem 7.6 (and Corollary 6.5 for the index bound) on $N$ with $P_{+}=\varnothing$ and $P_{-}=\partial N$ . ∎

#### Corollary 10.3.

If $h\in C^{\infty}_{\text{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^{n+1})$ for $3\leq n+1\leq 7$ satisfies

- (1) there exists a nonempty bounded set of finite perimeter $\Lambda$ satisfying $\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Lambda)\leq 0$ ,

- (2) $h(x)\leq C|x|^{-1-\alpha}$ for some $\alpha,\ C>0$ ,

then there exists a smooth closed almost embedded $h$ -PMC hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ with $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ -index at most 1.

#### Proof.

Choose $R$ so large that $\Lambda\subset B_{R}(0)$ and $h\mid_{\partial B_{R}(0)}\leq CR^{-1-\alpha}<n/R$ . Set $N=\overline{B_{R}(0)}$ , and note that $H_{\partial N,N}=n/R>h$ .

Let $\Phi_{0}(t)=\Lambda\cap B_{Rt}(0)$ . Then

$$ \max\{\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(0)),\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(1))\}=\max\{\mathcal{A}^{h}(\varnothing),\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Lambda)\}=0. $$

By the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality (and the fact that $h$ is bounded on $N$ ), we have $\mathbf{L}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(N))>0$ .

Hence, the conclusion follows from Theorem 10.1. ∎

### 11. Application II: CMC hypersurfaces in finite volume

We use the theory developed in Theorem 9.5 to provide new answers to Question 1.2.

#### 11.1. Isoperimetric profile

Let $(M,g)$ be a complete finite volume manifold.

#### Definition 11.1 (Isoperimetric profile).

For $v\in(0,\mathrm{Vol}(M))$ , we define

$$ \mathscr{I}(v)=\inf\{\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)\mid\Omega\in\mathcal{C}(M),\ \mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega)=v\}. $$

Since we assume $(M,g)$ has finite volume, $\mathscr{I}(v)>0$ for all $v\in(0,\mathrm{Vol}(M))$ and the infimum is achieved by a finite perimeter set (by [NR21, Theorem 2.2]), and $\mathscr{I}$ is continuous (by [NR21, Corollary 2.3]).

#### Definition 11.2.

We define

$$ \mathscr{D}(M,g):=\mathrm{Lip}(\mathscr{I})=\sup_{v_{1}\neq v_{2}}\left|\frac{\mathscr{I}(v_{2})-\mathscr{I}(v_{1})}{v_{2}-v_{1}}\right|. $$

#### Remark 11.3.

Since $\mathscr{I}(v)>0$ for finite volume manifolds, $\mathscr{D}(M,g)>0$ .

#### 11.2. Existence of CMC hypersurfaces

We now prove the main result of the subsection.

#### Theorem 11.4.

Let $(M,g)$ be a complete finite volume manifold of dimension $3\leq n+1\leq 7$ . If $0<c<\mathscr{D}(M,g)$ , then there is a smooth complete almost embedded $c$ -CMC hypersurface in $M$ with $\mathcal{A}^{c}$ -index at most 1.

#### Proof.

Since $\mathscr{I}$ is symmetric under $v\mapsto\mathrm{Vol}(M)-v$ , we can find $v_{1}<v_{2}$ so that

$$ \frac{\mathscr{I}(v_{1})-\mathscr{I}(v_{2})}{v_{2}-v_{1}}>c. $$

By Lemma 11.5 below, we can find $\Omega_{1}\in\mathcal{C}_{\varnothing}(M)$ with $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega_{1})$ approximately $v_{2}$ and

$$ \frac{\mathscr{I}(v_{1})-\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega_{1})}{\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega_{1})-v_{1}}\geq c+\delta $$

for some $\delta>0$ small.

Let $\Phi_{0}:[0,1]\to\mathcal{C}_{\varnothing}(M)$ be any $\mathbf{F}$ -continuous path from $\varnothing$ to $\Omega_{1}$ . Take $h=-c$ . Then $\varnothing$ is the unique minimizer of $\mathcal{A}^{h}$ . For any $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}_{\varnothing}(M)$ with $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega)=v_{1}$ , we have by (11.1)

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega) \displaystyle=\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)+c\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega) \displaystyle\geq\mathscr{I}(v_{1})+cv_{1} \displaystyle\geq\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega_{1})+c\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega_{1})+\frac{\delta}{2}(v_{2}-v_{1}) \displaystyle=\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Omega_{1})+\frac{\delta}{2}(v_{2}-v_{1}). $$

Hence, we have

$$ \mathbf{L}^{h}(\Pi_{\Phi_{0}})>\max\{\mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(0)),\ \mathcal{A}^{h}(\Phi_{0}(1))\}. $$

The theorem now follows from Theorem 9.5. ∎

#### Lemma 11.5.

For any $v\in(0,\mathrm{Vol}(M))$ and any $\varepsilon>0$ , there is a bounded set $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}(M)$ satisfying

$$ |\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega)-v|<\varepsilon\ \ \text{and}\ \ |\mathscr{I}(v)-\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)|<\varepsilon. $$

#### Proof.

Since $M$ has finite volume, there is $\{K_{i}\}_{i}$ a nested exhaustion by compact sets with smooth boundary satisfying $\limsup_{i\to\infty}\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial K_{i})=0$ .

Let $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}(M)$ satisfy $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega)=v$ and $\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)\leq\mathscr{I}(v)+\varepsilon/2$ . Let $\Omega_{i}=\Omega\cap K_{i}$ . Then

$$ \limsup_{i\to\infty}\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega_{i})\leq\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)+\limsup_{i\to\infty}\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial K_{i})=\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega), $$

$$ \liminf_{i\to\infty}\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega_{i})\geq\liminf_{i\to\infty}\mathcal{H}^{n}((\partial^{*}\Omega)\cap K_{i})=\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega). $$

Moreover,

$$ \limsup_{i\to\infty}\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega_{i})\leq\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega), $$

$$ \liminf_{i\to\infty}\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega_{i})\geq\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega)-\limsup_{i\to\infty}\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(M\setminus K_{i})=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega). $$

Hence, we can take $\Omega_{i}$ for $i$ sufficiently large (depending on $\varepsilon$ ). ∎

#### 11.3. Lower bounds for Lipschitz constant of isoperimetric profile

In the rest of the section, we develop tools to compute lower bounds for the invariant $\mathscr{D}$ . We conclude the subsection with a few examples.

#### Proposition 11.6.

Let $\delta\in(0,\mathrm{Vol}(M))$ . Suppose there are locally smooth functions

$$ \eta_{1}:(0,\delta)\to(0,+\infty),\ \ \eta_{2}:(0,\delta)\to(0,+\infty) $$

satisfying $\lim_{t\to 0}\eta_{j}(t)=0$ and $\mathscr{I}(v)\geq\min\{\eta_{1}(v),\eta_{2}(v)\}$ for all $v\in(0,\delta)$ . Then

$$ \mathscr{D}(M,g)\geq\min\left\{\liminf_{t\to 0}\eta_{1}^{\prime}(t),\ \liminf_{t\to 0}\eta_{2}^{\prime}(t)\right\}. $$

#### Proof.

Set $m=\min\left\{\liminf_{t\to 0}\eta_{1}^{\prime}(t),\ \liminf_{t\to 0}\eta_{2}^{\prime}(t)\right\}$ (unless the right hand side is $+\infty$ , in which case we set $m=1$ for convenience). If $m=0$ , then the conclusion is trivial, so we assume $m>0$ .

Fix $\varepsilon\in(0,m)$ . We claim that

$$ \min\{\eta_{1}(v),\eta_{2}(v)\}\geq(m-\varepsilon)v. $$

for all $v$ sufficiently small. Indeed, by the definition of $m$ , there is some $\sigma>0$ so that for all $t\in(0,\sigma)$ , we have $\eta_{j}^{\prime}(t)\geq m-\varepsilon$ for $j=1,2$ . By the fundamental theorem of calculus, we have $\eta_{j}(t)\geq(m-\varepsilon)t$ for all $t\in(0,\sigma)$ for $j=1,2$ , so the desired conclusion holds.

Hence, we have $\mathscr{I}(v)\geq(m-\varepsilon)v$ for any $v\in(0,\sigma)$ . Let $v_{2}\in(0,\sigma)$ . Since $\lim_{v\to 0}\mathscr{I}(v)=0$ , there is a sequence of positive real numbers $\{v_{1}^{i}\}_{i}$ converging to $0$ with $\mathscr{I}(v_{1}^{i})<\mathscr{I}(v_{2})$ . We have

$$ \displaystyle\mathscr{D}(M,g) \displaystyle\geq\liminf_{i\to\infty}\left|\frac{\mathscr{I}(v_{2})-\mathscr{I}(v_{1}^{i})}{v_{2}-v_{1}^{i}}\right| \displaystyle=\liminf_{i\to\infty}\frac{\mathscr{I}(v_{2})-\mathscr{I}(v_{1}^{i})}{v_{2}-v_{1}^{i}} \displaystyle\geq\liminf_{i\to\infty}\frac{\mathscr{I}(v_{2})-\mathscr{I}(v_{1}^{i})}{v_{2}} \displaystyle\geq m-\varepsilon. $$

Since $\varepsilon>0$ was arbitrary, the conclusion follows. ∎

Suppose $E\subset M$ is the complement of a precompact open subset with smooth boundary in $M$ . We define

$$ \mathscr{I}_{E}(v)=\inf\{\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)\mid\Omega\in\mathcal{C}(M),\ \Omega\subset E,\ \mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega)=v\}. $$

#### Proposition 11.7.

Suppose $E\subset M$ is the complement of a precompact open subset with smooth boundary in $M$ . Let $\delta\in(0,\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(E))$ . Suppose there is a locally smooth function

$$ \eta:(0,\delta)\to(0,+\infty) $$

satisfying $\lim_{t\to 0}\eta(t)=0$ and $\mathscr{I}_{E}(v)\geq\eta(v)$ for all $v\in(0,\delta)$ . Then

$$ \mathscr{D}(M,g)\geq\liminf_{t\to 0}\eta^{\prime}(t). $$

#### Proof.

If $\liminf_{t\to 0}\eta^{\prime}(t)=0$ , then the conclusion is trivial, so we assume otherwise.

Since $\partial E$ is smooth, compact, and separating, we can find a compact set $K\subset M$ with smooth boundary so that

- • $E\cup K=M$ ,

- • there is a diffeomorphism

$$ \phi:\partial E\times[0,\varepsilon]\to E\cap K $$

satisfying $\phi(\partial E,t)=\{x\in E\mid d(x,\partial E)=t\}$ .

Since $K$ is compact with smooth boundary, by [Rit23, Theorem 9.6] there are constants $C_{K},\ v_{K}>0$ so that for any $\Lambda\in\mathcal{C}(M)$ with $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Lambda\cap K)\leq v_{K}$ , we have

$$ \mathcal{H}^{n}((\partial^{*}\Lambda)\cap K)\geq C_{K}(\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Lambda\cap K))^{\frac{n}{n+1}}. $$

For $t\in[0,\varepsilon]$ , we let $S_{t}=\phi(\partial E,t)$ , $K_{t}=K\setminus\phi(\partial E,[t,\varepsilon])$ , and $E_{t}=E\setminus\phi(\partial E,[0,t])$ .

Fix $v\in(0,\delta)$ . By [NR21, Corollary 2.2] (since we assume $(M,g)$ has finite volume), we can find $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}(M)$ satisfying

$$ \mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega)=v\ \ \text{and}\ \ \mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)=\mathscr{I}(v). $$

Case 1: Suppose $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega\cap K)\geq v^{\frac{n+2}{n+1}}$ . By (11.2), we have (for $v$ sufficiently small)

$$ \mathscr{I}(v)=\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)\geq\mathcal{H}^{n}((\partial^{*}\Omega)\cap K)\geq C_{K}v^{\frac{n+2}{n+1}\frac{n}{n+1}}=C_{K}v^{\frac{n^{2}+2n}{n^{2}+2n+1}}=:\eta_{1}(v). $$

Case 2: Suppose $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega\cap K)\leq v^{\frac{n+2}{n+1}}$ . By the coarea formula in $E\cap K$ , there is a constant $c_{1}=c_{1}(E,K)>0$ so that for some $t\in[0,\varepsilon]$ (depending on $\Omega$ ), we have

$$ \mathcal{H}^{n}(\Omega\cap S_{t})\leq c_{1}v^{\frac{n+2}{n+1}}. $$

By assumption and the definition of $\mathscr{I}_{E}$ , we have

$$ \mathcal{H}^{n}((\partial^{*}\Omega)\cap E_{t})+\mathcal{H}^{n}(\Omega\cap S_{t})=\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}(\Omega\cap E_{t}))\geq\eta(\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega\cap E_{t})). $$

Since $\liminf_{t\to 0}\eta^{\prime}(t)>0$ , $\eta$ is increasing for $v$ sufficiently small. So for sufficiently small $v$ , by (11.4) and (11.5), we have

$$ \mathscr{I}(v)=\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)\geq\mathcal{H}^{n}((\partial^{*}\Omega)\cap E_{t})\geq\eta(v-v^{\frac{n+2}{n+1}})-c_{1}v^{\frac{n+2}{n+1}}=:\eta_{2}(v). $$

Hence, for $v$ sufficiently small, we have

$$ \mathscr{I}(v)\geq\min\{\eta_{1}(v),\eta_{2}(v)\}, $$

where $\eta_{1}$ and $\eta_{2}$ are as defined in (11.3) and (11.6). Since

$$ \liminf_{t\to 0}\eta_{1}^{\prime}(t)=+\infty\ \ \text{and}\ \ \liminf_{t\to 0}\eta_{2}^{\prime}(t)=\liminf_{t\to 0}\eta^{\prime}(t), $$

the conclusion follows by Proposition 11.6. ∎

We now compute lower bounds for $\mathscr{D}$ for a large class of finite volume manifolds with special structure outside a compact set.

#### Proposition 11.8.

Let $(M^{n+1},g)$ be a complete manifold with finite volume and dimension $3\leq n+1\leq 7$ . Suppose there is a compact set $K\subset M$ so that $M\setminus K$ is isometric to

$$ ((A,\infty)\times N,\ \psi^{2}(t)dt^{2}\oplus\rho^{2}(t)g_{N}) $$

for a fixed closed Riemannian manifold $(N^{n},g_{N})$ of dimension $n$ and locally smooth positive functions $\psi$ and $\rho$ . If $\rho^{\prime}<0$ and $\frac{\rho^{\prime}}{\rho\psi}$ is nonincreasing, then

$$ \mathscr{D}(M,g)\geq-n\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\rho^{\prime}(t)}{\rho(t)\psi(t)}. $$

#### Proof.

In the provided coordinates, we let $E=[A+1,\infty)\times N$ .

Take any $v\in(0,\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(E))$ . Let $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}(M)$ with $\Omega\subset E$ satisfy (by [NR21, Corollary 2.2])

$$ \mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega)=v\ \ \text{and}\ \ \mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)=\mathscr{I}_{E}(v). $$

Let $\Omega_{t}=\Omega\cup([t,\infty)\times N)$ . Since $\Omega$ has finite perimeter and $M$ has finite volume, we have

$$ \lim_{t\to\infty}\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega_{t})=\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega)\ \ \text{and}\ \ \lim_{t\to\infty}\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega_{t})=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega_{t}). $$

Let $O_{t}$ be the subset of the form $[\tau_{t},\infty)\times N$ so that $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(O_{t})=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega_{t})$ .

Let

$$ \omega=\rho^{n}\mathrm{vol}_{N}. $$

Then

$$ d\omega=n\rho^{n-1}\rho^{\prime}dt\wedge\mathrm{vol}_{N}=n\frac{\rho^{\prime}}{\rho\psi}\mathrm{vol}_{M}. $$

By Stokes’ theorem, we have

$$ \displaystyle\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial O_{t})-\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega_{t}) \displaystyle\leq\int_{[\partial O_{t}]}\omega-\int_{[\partial^{*}\Omega_{t}]}\omega \displaystyle=\int_{[O_{t}]-[\Omega_{t}]}d\omega \displaystyle=\int_{O_{t}\setminus\Omega_{t}}n\frac{\rho^{\prime}}{\rho\psi}-\int_{\Omega_{t}\setminus O_{t}}n\frac{\rho^{\prime}}{\rho\psi} $$

Since $O_{t}$ has the same volume as $\Omega_{t}$ , we have $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(O_{t}\setminus\Omega_{t})=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega_{t}\setminus O_{t})$ . Moreover, by assumption,

$$ n\frac{\rho^{\prime}}{\rho\psi}\Big|_{O_{t}\setminus\Omega_{t}}\leq n\frac{\rho^{\prime}}{\rho\psi}\Big|_{\Omega_{t}\setminus O_{t}}. $$

Hence, we have

$$ \mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial O_{t})\leq\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega_{t}). $$

Taking $t\to\infty$ , we have

$$ \mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial O)\leq\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial^{*}\Omega), $$

where $O$ is the subset of the form $[\tau,\infty)\times N$ with $\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(O)=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}(\Omega)=v$ , so

$$ \mathscr{I}_{E}(v)=\mathcal{H}^{n}(\partial O). $$

In other words, the areas and volumes of the subsets of the form $[\tau,\infty)\times N$ provide a lower bound for $\mathscr{I}_{E}$ .

Let $a(t)=\mathcal{H}^{n}(\{t\}\times N)$ and $v(t)=\mathcal{H}^{n+1}([t,\infty)\times N)$ . If $t(v)$ denotes the inverse function of $v(t)$ , we have

$$ \eta(v)=a(t(v)) $$

is a lower bound for $\mathscr{I}_{E}$ . By the coarea formula and the formula for the derivative of an inverse function, we have

$$ \eta^{\prime}(v)=\frac{n\rho^{n-1}\rho^{\prime}}{-\rho^{n}\psi}=-n\frac{\rho^{\prime}}{\rho\psi}. $$

The conclusion follows by Proposition 11.7. ∎

We now compute lower bounds for $\mathscr{D}$ for a few examples.

#### Example 11.9 (Finite volume hyperbolic manifolds).

Let $(M,g)$ be a complete hyperbolic manifold with finite volume. By the structure theorem for these manifolds (see [Thu97, Chapter 4.5]), there is a compact set $K\subset M$ , a constant $A>0$ , and a closed Riemannian manifold $(N,g_{N})$ (a union of flat tori and flat Klein bottles) so that $M\setminus K$ is isometric to

$$ ((A,\infty)\times N,t^{-2}dt^{2}\oplus t^{-2}g_{N}). $$

In this case, $\psi(t)=\rho(t)=t^{-1}$ . We see that

$$ \rho^{\prime}=-t^{-2}<0\ \ \text{and}\ \ \frac{\rho^{\prime}}{\rho\psi}=-1\ \ \text{is nonincreasing}. $$

By Proposition 11.8, we have

$$ \mathscr{D}(M,g)\geq n. $$

By Theorem 11.4, we have Corollary 1.7.

#### Example 11.10 ( $\mathscr{D}=+\infty$ ).

Let $(N,g_{N})$ be a closed Riemannian manifold. Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold isometric to

$$ ((A,\infty)\times N,dt^{2}\oplus e^{-2t^{1+\alpha}}g_{N}) $$

outside a compact set, where $\alpha>0$ . Completeness follows from construction, and the fact that $M$ has finite volume follows because

$$ \int_{1}^{\infty}e^{-nt^{1+\alpha}}dt\leq\int_{1}^{\infty}e^{-nt}dt=\frac{-1}{n}e^{-nt}\Big|_{1}^{\infty}=\frac{e^{-n}}{n}. $$

In this case, we have $\psi(t)=1$ and $\rho(t)=e^{-t^{1+\alpha}}$ . We compute

$$ \rho^{\prime}=-(1+\alpha)t^{\alpha}e^{-t^{1+\alpha}}<0 $$

and

$$ \frac{\rho^{\prime}}{\rho\psi}=-(1+\alpha)t^{\alpha}\ \ \text{is nonincreasing}. $$

By Proposition 11.8, we have

$$ \mathscr{D}(M,g)\geq\lim_{t\to\infty}n(1+\alpha)t^{\alpha}=+\infty. $$

By Theorem 11.4, we can find a smooth complete almost embedded finite area $c$ -CMC hypersurface in $M$ for any $0<c<\infty$ .
